Implemented and merged across framework + cloud:

- **framework** #2181 (merged, main `e411a8219`) — `surface` on SkillSchema/AgentSchema; `ask` persona split (dropped the unified INTENT-FIRST classifier + `buildRegisterActive` shim); `schema_reader` (surface:'both') for the shared reads; affinity enforced as a load error in `resolveActiveSkills`; `agent` type `allowRuntimeCreate:false, allowOrgOverride:false` + catalog filtered to platform agents; `data-chat-agent.ts`→`ask-agent.ts`.
- **cloud** objectstack-ai/cloud#417 (merged, main `3d72d8790`) — `build` agent `surface:'build'` + attaches `schema_reader`; `metadata_authoring`/`solution_design` → `surface:'build'`; stopped dual-listing the shared reads; dropped the custom-agent guidance.
- **objectui** — no change needed: surface binding (alias groups, isBuildAgent/isAskAgent, aiStudio gate, hidden picker) already in place.

Checklist: persona split ✅, naming ✅, surface field + backfill ✅, tool scoping (no global fall-through; tools(ask) carries no authoring tools — asserted) ✅, withdraw tenant agents ✅. **D4** left deferred per the issue.

Note: several items were already done in main ahead of the ADR text (the ask rename; the resolver was already skill-scoped; build was already canonical+aliased). The cloud .framework-sha bump also required binding 18 control-plane script actions to satisfy framework's unrelated new action-script guard.

Keeping this as the **single live tracker** for ADR-0063/0064; closed #2165 (the near-duplicate follow-up) as superseded.

The code split is done (this issue's checklist + #2181 + cloud#417). The one tail this was reopened for — the **prose sweep / `surface` documentation** — was the third-party skill-authoring contract `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, which still described the old ADR-0040 *unified `data_chat` assistant*. That's fixed in **#2194**:

- SKILL.md rewritten to the two surface-bound agents (`ask`/`build`); `data_chat`/`metadata_assistant` reduced to alias-table mentions only.
- `surface: 'ask'|'build'|'both'` field + built-in skill affinities documented; tools = union of surface-compatible skills' tools (no global fall-through).
- `surface:'build'` skills documented as **inert on OSS — intentional tiering**, with graceful build-intent degradation.
- `docs/adr/PRIORITIZATION.md` stale 0040 row reconciled.

After #2194 merges, the only outstanding item is **D4** (deployment guardrail-floor), which remains **deferred** (no tenant agent to floor once withdrawal landed). Suggest closing this once #2194 is in and the D4 deferral is acknowledged.

All 13 checklist items are done; ticked above. Summary:

- **Code (this repo):** #2181 — persona split, `surface` field + skill backfill, `schema_reader` (both), no global fall-through, affinity load error, `agent` type closed (`allowRuntimeCreate:false`), catalog filtered, `ask-agent.ts` rename. Alias ESM/CJS sharing follow-up in #2190.
- **Cloud:** cloud#417 — `build` canonical + `metadata_assistant` permanent alias, build skills `surface:'build'`, dropped `app.defaultAgent` guidance. _(Cross-repo; please confirm from the cloud repo — not visible here.)_
- **objectui:** surface binding / hidden picker / graceful build-agent absence already in place (#1868, #1873).
- **Docs tail (what this was reopened for):** the third-party skill-authoring contract `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` still described the old ADR-0040 unified `data_chat` assistant — fixed in **#2194** (merged `9796cee4`): rewritten to the `ask`/`build` two-surface model, `surface` field documented, `surface:'build'` documented as inert-on-OSS (intentional tiering), `PRIORITIZATION.md` 0040 row reconciled.

Duplicate follow-up #2165 closed as superseded by this issue.

**D4** (deployment guardrail-floor schema) remains **deferred** — no tenant agent to floor once withdrawal landed; tracked in the audit (`docs/audits/2026-06-ask-build-agent-development-assessment.md`), not blocking.

Closing — ADR-0063/0064 fully landed bar the deferred D4.

⚠️ Closing `not_planned` — **the premise of this card is falsified.** PM `session_01FGca3Gt5irhBoVcVwFfoVY`, 2026-09-10T09:0xZ. Correction is on me, not on anyone who read it.

This card said `EnvSettingsRoutesPlugin` is an orphan workaround that exists only because cloud#1963 req 6 forbade framework changes, and that the next host door should go through the framework's `registerDomainHandler` instead of copying it.

The second half is wrong, measured on `origin/main`. objectstack `dd2184a` (#16741, merged 2026-09-08) built exactly that next host door — `mountStorageRoutes`, for kernels with no `http-server` — and its docblock names the settings bridge as the **working precedent it followed**, verbatim:

> The settings service already has a working answer to the same shape: the host mounts `registerSettingsRoutes` on its raw app and dispatches into the environment kernel's route table.

It did **not** use `registerDomainHandler`, did not add a `/storage` dispatcher domain, and did not touch `route-ledger.ts`. So the shape this card called an orphan is the shape the framework adopted; the only thing #16741 changed is that the composition of the gates now lives inside the owning package rather than on the host's side, which is a refinement of the same pattern, not a replacement for it.

⇒ There is nothing to migrate and nothing to warn the next card away from. Leaving this card open would actively mis-route the next host door.

**Why I got it wrong:** the checkout I read is pinned at `8b37a09` (2026-09-08T03:59Z), 288 commits behind `origin/main`; #16741 merged about two hours after that pin. Every framework reading in this card, and in the comment I posted on #1969 the same day, is accurate for that tree and stale for today's. See objectstack#17354 for the same correction on the framework side.

⛔ Do not reopen this as a "migrate the settings door" card without a fresh reading — as of `origin/main` today there is no divergence to close.
